Ravi: Quick follow-up on the FP8/INT8 migration RFC — saw a few edge cases in the canary that I want to sync on. Can we agree on a single "anchor" metric and a concrete backstop policy?
Hao: +1. Which anchor do you have in mind? latency or quality? we need something that surfaces subtle regressions.
Marta: degscore worked well in past runs. but degscore drift can be noisy on short tests. maybe degscore + an absolute task-level metric for core tasks.
Ben: For NER/classif endpoints we can use F1 delta (relative) + degscore. For generation endpoints maybe ROUGE-L or ppl on heldout prompts. Keep the backstop simple: if anchor crosses threshold then auto-roll back.
Ravi: proposal: primary anchor = degscore (sensitive to hallucinations), secondary anchors = task-specific metric (F1/ROUGE/ppl). Backstop: if primary anchor degrades > 1.2x baseline AND any secondary anchor degrades > 1% absolute -> rollback.
Hao: sounds reasonable. Can we make the thresholds configurable per-customer? enterprise customers might tolerate less.
Marta: yes, per-customer overrides. but runtime needs an unambiguous fail flag from the canary job. ops-bot should surface the exact signal.
ops-bot: canary run 1775001234-started by @Ravi. collecting metrics: degscore, rouge_l, f1, latency_p50.
Ben: also we need a short window check for high-confidence token regressions. small absolute drops on common tokens should be caught.
Ravi: true — add token-top-100 frequency match as a lightweight heuristic. If token-match drops > 0.5% absolute -> mark as degradation signal (counts towards secondary anchors).
Hao: how do we encode this in the rollout config? propose a tiny DSL per endpoint:
```
rollout_policy:
  anchor_primary: degscore
  primary_threshold: 1.2
  secondary_checks:
    - name: rouge_l
      delta_abs: 0.01
    - name: token_top100
      delta_abs: 0.005
  per_customer_override: true
```
Marta: that works. runtime should emit a single boolean `canary_pass` plus a JSON blob of metrics for audit. If `canary_pass` false -> automatic rollback and alert to #eng-oncall.
Ben: add a hysteresis: require 2 consecutive failing canaries within 3 hours before rollback for non-critical customers. Critical customers (SLA) should rollback immediately.
Ravi: agree. add `hysteresis_count` + `customer_tier` in the policy. Also we need a short playbook for manual review when signals conflict (primary pass but secondary fail).
Hao: I'll draft a PR to the rollout service that adds these fields and emits the canary_pass flag. Will include unit tests for the token-top-100 calculation.
Marta: I'll add the monitoring alert groups and notebook to reproduce the degscore baseline.
Ben: I'll update the ops-runbook (canary -> rollback flow) and add steps for manual QA.
Ravi: sweet. owners: Hao (service change), Marta (monitoring + baseline), Ben (runbook). ops-bot, please reopen thread with canary summary once the PR lands. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: acknowledged. will post canary_summary on merge.
